messages.subject: Simulating SEM data
parts:
I'm trying to create simulated datasets to test the differences that occur under different model structures. I'm using simsem in R to do this and have had no luck getting it to actually simulate the datasets successfully. I need to generate datasets that have nine indicators (x1 - x9) used to measure a multidimensional latent variable (D) that has three dimensions (A, B, C). Factor A is measured by x1, x2, x3. Factor B is measured by x4, x5, x6.  Factor C is measured by x7, x8, x9. Y is regressed on D. The lower-order factor loadings should all be set to .4, the higher-order factor loadings should all be set to .5, and the strength of the path coefficient between D --> Y should be set to .25, all as shown below. I also want to calculate three parcels in the datasets, each calculated based on the averages specified in the measurement portion of the model below. I've been using the following syntax:

# Load packages
library(simsem)
library(lavaan)

set.seed(12345)

# Sim data model
simModel <- '
  # Measurement
  A =~ 0.4*x1 + 0.4*x2 + 0.4*x3
  B =~ 0.4*x4 + 0.4*x5 + 0.4*x6
  C =~ 0.4*x7 + 0.4*x8 + 0.4*x9
 
  # Parcels
  P123 = (x1 + x2 + x3)/3
  P456 = (x4 + x5 + x6)/3
  P789 = (x7 + x8 + x9)/3

  # Structural
  D =~ 0.5*A + 0.5*B + 0.5*C
  Y ~ 0.25*D
 
  # Variances
  A ~~ 0.75*A
  B ~~ 0.75*B
  C ~~ 0.75*C
  '

# Homogeneous fit model
fit_hom <- '
  # Measures
  A =~ P123
  B =~ P456
  C =~ P789
  D =~ A + B + C

  Y ~ D
  '

# Run simulation with N = 500
simOutput_1 <- sim(
  nRep = 1500,
  model = fit_hom,
  n = 500,
  generate = simModel,
  lavaanfun = 'lavaan',
  se = 'standard'
)

When I run the above, it tells me:
Progress: 1 / 1500 Error in str2lang(x) : <text>:1:40: unexpected symbol 1: ~ 0.4*x7+0.4*x8+0.4*x9P123=(x1+x2+x3)/3P456

I am having trouble determining what is going wrong. I suspect I am goofing something up in the simModel or have omitted something critical in my fitModel, but I am not certain. Any insight from anyone that could help me troubleshoot this so that I can get it to work successfully would be extremely appreciated. This is my first time doing this, so it would be so helpful. Thank you!

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Simulating SEM data
parts:
I am not familiar with simsem::sim(). I did a quick check and I think you can try the following suggestions:

- Remove these lines from simModel. They are not valid model syntax lines. They led to the error you encountered.

P123 = (x1 + x2 + x3)/3
  P456 = (x4 + x5 + x6)/3
  P789 = (x7 + x8 + x9)/3

- If you want to create parcels on the generated dataframe, write a function that has this form, and pass it to the datafun argument of sim():

create_parcels <- function(dat_i) {
  # dat_i is the data generated form simModel
  # Create parcels
  # Return a dataframe with the parcels.
}

The call should be something like this:

simOutput_1 <- sim(
 ...
 datafun = create_parcels,
 ...
)

- Something's wrong with fit_hom. A, B, and C are one-indicator factors. Is this what you want?

  D =~ P123 + P456 + P789

To check fit_hom, you can test it using only one dataset first:

data_test <- simulateData(simModel,
                          sample.nobs = 500,
                          seed = 1234)
fit <- sem(fit_hom, data = data_test)

Revise fit_hom until it works as expected for one dataset. You can then call sim().

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Simulating SEM data
parts:
In order to simulate from an item-level model, you must pass your population model syntax to the sim(generate=) function.  As Shu Fai pointed out, you cannot calculate new variables (composite scores or "parcels") in lavaan model syntax.  To transform your generated data, you can write a custom function with a data= argument, that calculates the composites and returns the updated data.frame.  You pass that function to the sim(datafun=) argument, described on the help page.  Then your sim(model=) argument can be your parcel-level model syntax.
